still_wrong.title: Scratches on steep walls come back while the deformation plays (user's case, default mesh)
still_wrong.detail: At rest the Im H = 0 contour on the left wall is now straight in light and dark (sin √z, t = 0.2, All sheets), so pictures-2 is fixed at rest. While the deformation plays it is not. At t ≈ 0.21 to 0.26, the same contour on the left salmon wall turns into a column of short white scratches. The Im H ≈ −0.5 contour on the cyan wall next to it becomes a sawtooth with a spark at its end. This happens with All sheets on and off, in 2 of 2 separate play runs. The likely cause is the moving path: its levels are stale (a frame or two late) or capped, and over 256 cells it uses the base heights. So walls are drawn with coarse chords while the contour is drawn at the exact F. That is the zigzag the ledger traced to the cap, now showing in motion. Playing the deformation is how the user meets this case. The rule is to never trade image quality for speed.
still_wrong.evidence: review-verify/play-wall-scratches-t0.24-allsheets-vs-principal-4x.png (left: All sheets at t = 0.236, right: principal at t = 0.256, both playing); play-vs-rest-left-wall-4x.png (left: playing at t = 0.21, right: the same wall at rest at t = 0.2, clean); play-t0.24-allsheets-vs-principal.png (whole pane); rest-t0.2-left-wall-contour-straight-4x.png (rest, light and dark).
still_wrong.fix: While moving, draw contours on refined or wall cells only where the facet is within a pixel of the true height. Elsewhere fade the contour out, as round 2 did before the fix, or take its height from the facet. Or keep the levels current while playing, without a synchronous read (they can be computed on the GPU from the same pass). Gate: on the user's frame captured mid-play at t ≈ 0.2, the left-wall contour deviates from a fitted line by at most 0.5 px.

still_wrong.title: Cold open with All sheets still splits into two or three stalls, the worst 1.09 s
still_wrong.detail: Principal surface (sheets off): fixed. In 5 build runs the longest main-thread gaps were 0, 0, 0, 376 and 393 ms. In 5 base runs they were 0, 0, 0, 209 (+136) and 172 ms. landTF, landNrm, floor and land are first used in the same millisecond. With All sheets on (7 build and 7 base runs, alternating), the principal programs and the sheets' programs are first drawn in different frames, 600 to 700 ms apart. For example, landTF@269 then landSheetTF@985, or landSheetTF@287 then landTF@1037. Each pays its own stall. Longest gap, build: 111, 1089, 415, 707, 535, 0, 0 ms. Base: 879, 612, 204, 633, 531, 162, 0 ms. In the worst pair (log(z²+c)), the build stalled 588 then 1089 ms and first showed the surface at 2069 ms. The base stalled 612 ms once and showed the surface at 1106 ms. A run that started with the sheets' programs (sqrt(z²+c), log(z⁴+c)) had no stall at all. So the ordering, not the shaders, splits the stall. The builder's cold test ran with sheets off only, and AS-BUILT lists the All-sheets cold open as not measured. The user's case uses All sheets.
still_wrong.evidence: review-verify/cold-principal-and-allsheets.out.json (10 principal and 4 All-sheets runs), cold-allsheets.out.json (10 All-sheets runs). Each line gives the gaps over 100 ms and the first-use times of each program.
still_wrong.fix: With All sheets on, do not draw the principal surface while the sheets' programs compile. Or put both families in one compile and link group, so that every first draw lands in one frame, as in the base. Add All sheets to the cold-open gate: 6 + 6 runs alternating, and the build's longest gap must be no worse than the base's.

still_wrong.title: BUDGET60: the Max mesh while playing (principal surface) still has p95 about 31 to 44 ms against the base's 17 to 18
still_wrong.detail: Desktop 1440x900, sin √z Im, playing, Max mesh, sheets off, 3 runs each. Build: 58.0 / 60.0 / 59.4 fps, p95 44.0 / 34.9 / 30.8 ms, max 49.9 / 42.6 / 46.3. Base: 60 fps, p95 17.3 / 17.3 / 18.3. Phone emulation (390x844, Max, principal, 2 runs): build p95 28.5 / 19.4 against base 18.2 / 18.7. The mean holds 60 fps, but 5 to 10 % of frames take two vsyncs, which is visible stutter. The ledger's own perf_desktop.out.json also has a Max run at p95 42.1 ms (All sheets). What now passes: All sheets at Max plays at 60 fps, p95 17.4 to 18.3, better than the base (45 to 50 fps). The default mesh passes everywhere, desktop and phone, light and dark. Orbiting tan z Re passes at both meshes.
still_wrong.fix: Profile the Max principal path while playing. The spikes look periodic: perhaps a fenced read landing and the groups being rebuilt (three transform-feedback passes per group) in the same frame. Spread the rebuild over frames or skip it while T changes. Gate the Max mesh while playing at p95 within base +0.5 ms, three runs.

still_wrong.title: All-sheets refinement is still capped for a heavy map, and Max then refines less than the default mesh
still_wrong.detail: The user's case is now uncapped at rest: 13.1 M evaluations at the default mesh, 17.2 M at Max, Lc 4. The principal case, tan z Re and sec z Re are uncapped too. But z^{1/5} tan 3z with All sheets, Re, is capped. At the default mesh it drops 1 level (9.4 M of 38.0 M needed). At Max it drops 2 levels and spends only 4.15 M of the 18 M budget. The uniform drop overshoots by 4x per level, so at Max the walls get 16x the chord error (about 4 px instead of 0.25) and fewer evaluations than at the default mesh. Choosing a finer mesh makes these walls coarser.
still_wrong.fix: After the uniform drop, spend what is left of the budget, for example by raising the worst cells back one level until the budget is full. At least never let Max refine less than the default mesh.

still_wrong.fix: As in pictures-3 and math-7: sample Im log log z per sheet on a small circle around z = 1, and run the hole and curtain check on GLR.landRefine(true).sheets.
